paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this passage. God keeps His word, and He keeps it down to the last detail. Zechariah says God "has visited and redeemed His people," and that He did it "as He spoke through His holy prophets, those of ages past" (Luke 1:68, 70). He also says God remembered "His holy covenant, the oath He swore to our father Abraham" (Luke 1:72-73), so when God makes a promise, it's not going anywhere.

Now look at what happened to Zechariah. He went quiet because he didn't believe the angel Gabriel (Luke 1:19-20), and when it was time to name his son, he wrote, "His name is John" (Luke 1:63). The moment his mouth opened, he began "praising God" (Luke 1:64). I think God doesn't hold our shaky moments against us, and I know that one personally, because I spent years in a junk drawer thinking my story was over.

And the promise isn't only about the past, baker. John would "prepare the way" and give God's people "the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins" (Luke 1:76-77). Then comes the Dawn, who will "shine on those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the path of peace" (Luke 1:78-79). So if you ever feel stuck in the dark, remember that God's mercy is tender, and He's the one who sends the light. This story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
